1.text_clean:
1. The graph shows the relationship between two quantities $p$ and $q$. The gradient of the graph is $r$ and the intercept on the $p$ axis is $s$.
[Graph: straight line of positive gradient, $p$ against $q$, intercept $s$ on the $p$ axis]
Which of the following is the correct relationship between $p$ and $q$?
A. $p = sq + r$
B. $p = rq + s$
C. $p = rq - s$
D. $p = rs + q$

2.text_clean:
2. The acceleration of free fall $g$ is determined by the relationship $g = \frac{4\pi^2 l}{t^2}$. The uncertainty in the value of $l$ is 2% and the uncertainty in the value of $t$ is 5%. What is the uncertainty in $g$?
A. 3%
B. 7%
C. 8%
D. 12%

3.text_clean:
3. Three coplanar forces of 5 N, 6 N and 7 N act on an object. Which force could not be the resultant of these three forces?
A. 0 N
B. 11 N
C. 13 N
D. 19 N

4.text_clean:
4. An object is thrown upwards leaving the thrower's hand at time $t = 0$. Which graph shows how speed $v$ varies with $t$ as the object rises and falls?
[Graphs of $v$ against $t$: A. straight-line V shape, falling linearly to zero then rising linearly; B. inverted V starting from zero; C. U-shaped curve touching zero; D. inverted parabola starting and ending at zero]

5.text_clean:
5. A ball of mass $m$ travels horizontally with speed $v$ before colliding with a vertical wall. The ball rebounds at speed $v$ in a direction opposite to its initial direction. What is the magnitude of the change in momentum of the ball?
A. 0
B. $\frac{mv}{2}$
C. $mv$
D. $2mv$

6.text_clean:
6. Balls X and Y are at the same height. X is projected horizontally at the same time that Y is dropped. Y is the same size as X but has half its mass.
[Diagram: balls Y and X side by side above the ground, X with a horizontal arrow]
Ignoring air resistance, which statement is true?
A. Y will hit the ground before X.
B. Y will hit the ground after X.
C. Y will hit the ground at the same time as X.
D. The outcome can only be determined if the initial speed of X is known.

7.text_clean:
7. A speed boat tows a water skier so that the skier accelerates.
[Diagram: speed boat towing a water skier by a tow rope]
The magnitude of the force exerted on the skier by the tow rope must be
I. greater than the magnitude of the total resistive force acting on the skier
II. equal to the magnitude of the force exerted on the tow rope by the skier
III. equal to the magnitude of the force causing the boat to accelerate.
Which of the above factors is/are correct?
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II only
D. III only

8.text_clean:
8. The internal energy of any substance is made up of the
A. total random kinetic and potential energy of its molecules.
B. total potential energy of its molecules.
C. total random kinetic energy of its molecules.
D. total vibrational energy of its molecules.

9.text_clean:
9. Energy is supplied at a constant rate to a fixed mass of a solid substance until it starts to boil. The graph shows how its temperature $T$ varies with time $t$.
[Graph: $T$/°C against $t$/s; solid heats from 0 °C at 0 s to 80 °C at 200 s; constant at 80 °C from 200 s to 500 s; liquid heats from 80 °C at 500 s to 120 °C at 900 s]
What is the value of the ratio $\frac{\text{specific latent heat of fusion}}{\text{specific heat capacity of substance in the liquid state}}$?
A. 20 K
B. 30 K
C. 40 K
D. 50 K

10.text_clean:
10. The diagram shows a $P$–$V$ cycle for a particular gas.
[Diagram: P–V cycle; 1→2 curved compression at lower pressure, 2→3 vertical (constant volume) pressure increase, 3→4 curved expansion, 4→1 vertical pressure decrease]
In which of the following changes is no work being done?
A. 1 → 2
B. 1 → 2 → 3
C. 1 → 2 → 3 → 4
D. 2 → 3

11.text_clean:
11. An ideal gas expands adiabatically. What energy change is true for the gas?
A. It gains thermal energy from the surroundings
B. It loses thermal energy to the surroundings
C. Its internal energy increases
D. Its internal energy decreases

12.text_clean:
12. Water in a container freezes. Which of the following correctly describes the change in entropy of the water and its surroundings?
Change in entropy of water | Change in entropy of surroundings
A. decrease | decrease
B. decrease | increase
C. increase | decrease
D. increase | increase

13.text_clean:
13. An object undergoes simple harmonic motion. Which graph shows the relationship between the acceleration $a$ and the displacement $x$ from the equilibrium position?
[Graphs of $a$ against $x$ through the origin: A. straight line of negative gradient; B. straight line of positive gradient; C. curve of negative slope steepening at the ends; D. curve of positive slope steepening at the ends]

14.text_clean:
14. Progressive (travelling) waves S and T have the same frequency and are in the same medium. S has amplitude 2.0 m and T has amplitude 4.0 m. What is the ratio of the intensity of T to the intensity of S?
A. $\frac{1}{4}$
B. $\frac{1}{2}$
C. 2
D. 4

15.text_clean:
15. Waves emitted from sources X and Y have equal wavelengths and are initially in phase. The waves interfere destructively at point P, where the path difference is 0.60 m.
[Diagram: sources X and Y and point P]
What is a possible value for the wavelength of the waves?
A. 0.20 m
B. 0.30 m
C. 0.40 m
D. 0.60 m

16.text_clean:
16. P and Q are two points on a standing wave. R and S are two points on a progressive (travelling) wave.
[Diagram: standing wave loop with adjacent points P and Q near an antinode; progressive wave with adjacent points R and S near a crest]
Which of the following gives the relationship between the amplitudes of each pair of points?
Points P and Q | Points R and S
A. same amplitude | same amplitude
B. different amplitude | same amplitude
C. same amplitude | different amplitude
D. different amplitude | different amplitude

17.text_clean:
17. A siren on an ambulance emits sound of frequency $f$. The speed of sound in still air is $v$. What is the frequency of the sound observed when the ambulance travels at speed $\frac{v}{10}$ towards a stationary observer?
A. $\frac{f}{10}$
B. $f$
C. $\frac{11}{10}f$
D. $\frac{10}{9}f$

18.text_clean:
18. Unpolarized light is incident on the surface of a transparent medium. The reflected light is completely plane polarized. The refracted light will be
A. unpolarized.
B. partially plane polarized.
C. completely plane polarized at right angles to the reflected light.
D. completely plane polarized parallel to the reflected light.

19.text_clean:
19. An electron has a kinetic energy of $4.8 \times 10^{-10}$ J. What is the equivalent value of this kinetic energy?
A. 3.0 eV
B. 3.0 keV
C. 3.0 MeV
D. 3.0 GeV
19.note: eV/J energy unit conversion; tagged X.1 (units)

20.text_clean:
20. An ideal ammeter is used to measure the current in a resistor. Which of the following gives the resistance of an ideal ammeter and the way it is connected to the resistor?
Resistance | Connection
A. infinite | in parallel
B. infinite | in series
C. zero | in parallel
D. zero | in series

21.text_clean:
21. The graph shows the variation of potential difference across a device with the current in the device.
[Graph: potential difference against current, curve rising with increasing gradient; point X at current $I$ and potential difference $V$]
Which of the following gives the resistance of the device at point X?
A. $\frac{V}{I}$
B. $\frac{I}{V}$
C. gradient of tangent to curve at X
D. $\frac{1}{\text{gradient of tangent to curve at X}}$

22.text_clean:
22. In the Geiger–Marsden experiment alpha particles were directed at a thin gold foil. Which of the following shows how the majority of the alpha particles behaved after reaching the foil?
[Diagrams of alpha particles approaching a foil: A. most pass straight through, one slightly deflected; B. all deflected through moderate angles; C. all reflected back; D. all stopped at the foil]

23.text_clean:
23. The diagram shows three electron energy levels of an atom. Which transition results in the emission of a photon of the longest wavelength?
[Energy level diagram: ground state and two upper levels; A. upward arrow from ground state to top level; B. upward arrow from middle level to top level; C. downward arrow from top level to ground state; D. downward arrow from top level to middle level]

24.text_clean:
24. The graph shows the relationship between binding energy per nucleon and nucleon number. In which region are nuclei most stable?
[Graph: binding energy per nucleon against nucleon number (0–250); region A at very low nucleon numbers on the steep rise, B on the upper part of the rise, C near the peak around 30–70, D at around 200–250]

25.text_clean:
25. For a black-body at absolute temperature $T$ the power emitted per unit area is $P$. What is the power emitted per unit area when the temperature is decreased to $\frac{1}{2}T$?
A. $\frac{P}{32}$
B. $\frac{P}{16}$
C. $\frac{P}{8}$
D. $\frac{P}{4}$

26.text_clean:
26. The SI unit of surface heat capacity is J m$^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$. Which unit is a correct alternative to this?
A. kg s$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$
B. kg s$^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$
C. kg s$^{-1}$ m$^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$
D. kg s$^{-2}$ m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$
26.note: audit: unit conversion only; no B.2 knowledge needed

27.text_clean:
27. Which of the following would not reduce the effects of the enhanced greenhouse effect?
A. Replacing natural gas power stations with those using oil
B. Replacing conventional vehicles with hybrid vehicles
C. Replacing fossil fuel power stations with those using nuclear fuel
D. Increasing the use of carbon dioxide capture and storage

28.text_clean:
28. The centres of two planets are separated by a distance $R$. The gravitational force between the two planets is $F$. What will be the force between the planets when their separation increases to $3R$?
A. $\frac{F}{9}$
B. $\frac{F}{3}$
C. $F$
D. $3F$

29.text_clean:
29. The acceleration of free fall of a mass of 2.0 kg close to the surface of Mars is 3.6 m s$^{-2}$. What is the gravitational field strength at the surface of Mars in N kg$^{-1}$?
A. 1.8
B. 3.6
C. 7.2
D. 9.8

30.text_clean:
30. A coil and a magnet can move horizontally to the left or to the right at the same speed.
[Diagram: bar magnet (S on left, N on right) next to a coil on its right; arrows show the conventional current direction in the coil leads]
In which of the following will a conventional current be induced in the direction shown in the diagram when both the magnet and the coil are moving?
direction of motion of magnet | direction of motion of coil
A. to the left | to the right
B. to the left | to the left
C. to the right | to the right
D. to the right | to the left

31.text_clean:
31. In an ideal transformer
I. the power output exceeds the power input
II. the magnetic flux produced by the primary coil entirely links the secondary coil
III. there are more turns on the secondary coil than on the primary coil.
Which of the above statements must be true?
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II only
D. III only

[Graph: sinusoidal $V$ against $t$, about three cycles]
Assuming all graph scales are identical, which graph shows the output when the speed of rotation is doubled?
[Graphs of $V$ against $t$: A. same amplitude, more cycles; B. double amplitude, double frequency; C. double amplitude, slightly more cycles; D. same amplitude, half the frequency]

A. time.
B. energy.
C. position.
D. mass.

A. Doubling the wavelength of the photons
B. Halving the wavelength of the photons
C. Doubling the number of photons incident on the surface per second
D. Halving the number of photons incident on the surface per second

A. an electric field only.
B. a magnetic field only.

B. Positron and antineutrino

A. 2
B. 4
C. 9
D. 15

A. charge stored by the device.
B. energy stored by the device.
